How can I resolve my traffic tickets?

If you have received a traffic ticket that is being handled by Sylvania Municipal Court, there are several options available to you for paying your fine. One option is to appear in person at the court's traffic bureau and pay your fine using cash, personal checks on banks within Lucas County, money orders, certified checks, MasterCard or Visa. Alternatively, you can pay your fine online by clicking on the provided link. It's important to note that all tickets must be paid before the court date listed on the bottom of your ticket to avoid incurring an additional $10 late fee.

If you prefer to mail in your payment, you can do so as long as it is received by the court prior to your court date (not the post-mark date). When mailing your payment, make sure to include the copy of your ticket with the waiver of court appearance signed, a check, money order or certified check made payable to Sylvania Municipal Court for the correct amount, and proof of insurance if you did not show it to the officer at the time you received the ticket. If you are appearing in court for a case at Sylvania Municipal Court, the Judge will inform you of your rights and the four available pleas that you can make during the court proceedings. These pleas include:

  1. Guilty
  2. No Contest
  3. Not Guilty

You will have the opportunity to make your plea in front of the Judge and the court, and it's important to understand the implications of each plea before making your choice. Despite the fact that online municipal case resolution is not currently offered by Sylvania Municipal Court, the court remains committed to providing the best possible service and support to its users, and is always exploring new ways to enhance its offerings and meet the needs of the community.

What is the role of the court clerk?

The Clerk of the Sylvania Municipal Court plays a vital role in the administration of justice at the court. The Clerk is responsible for maintaining separate records and dockets for both civil and criminal cases as required by law and ordered by the Court. All orders issued by the Court in these dockets are validated by the signature of the Judge or a facsimile thereof. In addition, the Clerk's office is authorized to grant only one continuance for a case. If you need to request a continuance, it's important to make the request yourself and not have a relative or friend call on your behalf. The continuance must also be requested within two weeks of your original court date. If you require a longer continuance, you will have to appear in court and make your request before the Judge on the record. Overall, the Clerk plays a crucial role in ensuring the smooth and efficient functioning of the Sylvania Municipal Court, and is a valuable resource for anyone seeking information or assistance with their case.

How can a marriage license be obtained?

If you are planning to get married and need to obtain a marriage license, the Sylvania Municipal Court follows Ohio's general marriage license law. This means that both parties must appear in person at the probate court and provide certain information under oath, including their name, age, residence, place of birth, occupation, Social Security number, father's name and mother's maiden name (if known), and the name of the person expected to solemnize the marriage (if known). Once this information is provided and the fee of $15 is paid, the court will issue a marriage license that is valid for 60 days from the date of issuance. It's important to note that the court does not provide marriage counseling or solemnize marriages, but can provide information about where to find a qualified officiant. Obtaining a marriage license from the Sylvania Municipal Court is a straightforward process that can be completed in person by both parties.

FAQs

What are the benefits of participating in the Specialized Drug Docket Program?

Obtain and maintain a sober lifestyle, improved life skills, personal relationships, stability in personal life, and reduce contacts with the criminal justice system.

How long will I be in the program?

The program is designed for twelve months but may be extended based on treatment needs or violations of rules and conditions.

How can I apply for the program?

A person must be recommended by the court prosecutor's office and undergo a diagnostic assessment and ORAS score determination.

What charges are eligible to be referred to the SDD program?

Misdemeanor offenses, drug-related offenses, moderate to high ORAS score, diagnosed substance abuse disorder, capable of participating and completing the program.

Who is not eligible for the SDD program?

Current charges carry mandatory jail days, related to firearm or deadly weapon, drug trafficking, violent or sexually oriented offenses, history of failures, pending cases in other courts.
